memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'For the land will be deserted by them and will enjoy its sabbaths while
it lies desolate without them. They will pay for their sin because they
rejected my laws and abhorred my decrees. Yet in spite of this, when they
are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or abhor them so
as to destroy them completely, breaking my covenant with them. I am the
LORD their God'" - Lev 26:43-44 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the most tender sentences in the entire chapter, and it
comes right at the end of all the warnings: "Yet in spite of this... I
will not reject them or abhor them so as to destroy them completely."

After all the rebellion, all the consequences, all the failure — God draws
a line He will not cross. He will discipline, but He will not annihilate.
He will scatter, but He will not finally abandon. His covenant will not be
broken, even when His people break faith.

Dear reader, sit in the warmth of that "yet." It is one of the most
beautiful words in Scripture. Your sin is real — "in spite of this" — but
God's commitment is greater. The whole chapter has been building to this
mercy that outlasts judgment.

This is the heart of God revealed across the whole Bible. Even when Israel
was faithless, Paul writes, God remains faithful, for He cannot disown
Himself (2 Tim 2:13). Lamentations, written amid the ruins of Jerusalem,
still declares: because of the LORD's great love we are not consumed, for
His compassions never fail (Lam 3:22).

For those in Christ, this security is complete. Nothing in all creation
can separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus (Rom 8:38-39).

Whatever you have done, hear the "yet" of God. His mercy is longer than
your failure. He will not let you go.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe God's commitment to me is greater than my failures?
2. What "yet" of God's mercy do I need to hear today?
3. How does God's covenant faithfulness give me security in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for Your "yet" — Your mercy that outlasts my failure. In
spite of all my sin, You will not let me go. Hold me secure in Christ.
Amen.
